business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Unitary National Jurisdiction – Registro Mercantil Central applicable nationwide)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European Doctrine with Regulatory Codification under Commercial Code of 1885 and Capital Companies Act 1/2010)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: DTAA Spain–Mexico (1992), Spain–Colombia (2005), Spain–Chile (2003), Spain–Peru (2005), Spain–Argentina (2013)
EU–Mexico Global Agreement and EU–Chile Advanced Framework Agreement (trade and investment facilitation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 6/2023 (transposing AMLD5) and developed by Real Decreto 304/2014; UBO transparency registers (Registro de Titularidades Reales) governed by Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio; corporate incorporation governed by Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital); name clearance governed by Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (RRM), Articles 403–414.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the corporate shareholder (Certificado de Vigencia of each non-resident corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or companies registrar in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Spain is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin) with subsequent sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the Spanish incorporation attorney or representative to execute the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin (or Spanish Consulate abroad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and certification by the Spanish Consulate where the country of origin is not an Apostille signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of passports and identity documents of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) and proposed directors/administrators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin or the Spanish Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable per country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / proof of funding source and asset origin issued for each UBO or corporate shareholder (certificado bancario de titularidad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille with sworn Spanish translation; originals accepted for amounts below €10,000 subject to enhanced verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (certificado de antecedentes penales) issued by the country of origin for each proposed manager/administrator (required for NIE formalities and fit-and-proper evaluation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national police authority of origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and sworn translation into Spanish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors, and beneficial persons against (i) the SEPBLAC risk indices and money-laundering typology guidelines, (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014, (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (iv) national domestic sanctions lists as gazetted by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, and (v) PEP databases meeting FATF Recommendations 12 and 22. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is compulsory where any UBO is a foreign or domestic Politically Exposed Person, where the transaction chain involves high-risk third countries identified by FATF, or where the source of funds for jewellery/fine-timepiece inventory exceeds EUR 10,000 per transaction. OFAC SDN screening is applied as market-standard best practice given USD-denominated settlement rails (Stripe/PayPal) and correspondent banking exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Online Name Certification Service (Solicitud de Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social), accessible at www.rmc.es or via the CertificaName / CIRCE portal auxiliary systems
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be rendered in Spanish using standard Latin script. Foreign words are admissible only when transliterated into phonetically pronounceable Spanish orthography and must not conflict with Spanish pronunciation rules. Accents and diacritics follow Real Academia Española norms; abbreviations, initials, and purely symbolic characters are restricted. The proposed name must be distinctive and not identical or grammatically/morphologically confusingly similar to any name already recorded in the centralized RMC index.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España / Spanish national symbols (requires prior authorization from the Ministry of the Presidency)
Gobierno, Ministerio, Ayuntamiento, Diputación or any token implying official public authority (prior ministerial approval required)
Banco, Caja, Financiera, Seguros, Reaseguros (reserved to supervised financial entities under Bank of Spain / DGSFP licensing)
Cooperativa, Mutualidad, Fundación (reserved to specific regulated legal forms)
Sociedad Anónima, S.A., Sociedad Limitada, S.L. as part of the name (mandatory type tokens excluded from the clearance request)
Unión Europea, Euro, Pax, Mundial or superlatives misleading as to scope or origin unless objectively justified
Names of provinces, municipalities, or autonomous communities where misleading as to geographic seat or government sponsorship
Internacional, Global, Holding, Multinacional unless the company can evidence objectively sufficient capital or group conditions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must submit a fresh application with up to three alternative proposed names (priority order). If the examiner refuses all alternatives, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice) within one month of notification, per Ley 39/2015, Articles 112–121. Exhaustion of administrative appeal permits subsequent judicial review before the Audiencia Nacional. No formal extension of a live negative-name certificate exists beyond the statutory 90-day window; however, a new certificate for the same name may be re-requested after the expiry date if the name remains unclaimed. Applicants are advised to secure clearance before signing the notarial deed, as the certification must be attached to the escritura de constitución.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are acknowledged for SL e-commerce structures provided the registered address serves as a genuine communication hub where official notifications (AEAT tax notices, Registro Mercantil correspondence, and judicial service) can be physically received and forwarded. For the online jewellery and fine timepieces segment, a purely letterbox address without any operational capacity is discouraged because Spanish customs (Agencia Tributaria – Departamento de Aduanas) and platform payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) may demand evidence of a real establishment, VAT registration address consistency, and returns-management capability. Industry-accepted practice: a serviced office with administrative reception, mail handling, and records custody for a minimum of 12 months satisfies current substance v. letterbox scrutiny at Stage 1.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-elevated risk – quantified at approximately 25–35% probability of an unannounced physical inspection or substance verification by AEAT, SEPBLAC, or the Registro Mercantil within the first 24 months of operations, given the high unit value of watches/fashion jewellery, cross-border e-commerce volumes, and the additional inspection powers introduced by Law 11/2021 regarding minimum substance requirements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name certificate (certificación de denominación social) – one primary plus two alternatives at the Registro Mercantil Central
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per RMC fee schedule (approx. EUR 13–15 per application)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association (escritura de constitución y estatutos sociales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Notary Public (Notaría) in Madrid or Barcelona
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (Arancel Notarial) calculated on capital and deed length; prevailing market rate for a minimum-capital SL with standard clauses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry registration filing (inscripción de la sociedad en el Registro Mercantil Provincial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registral tariff (Arancel de los Registradores de la Propiedad y Mercantiles) based on nominal capital and number of entries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign corporate good-standing certificates, passports, powers of attorney, and bank reference letters (estimated 4–6 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of origin country and/or Spanish Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee per document (approx. EUR 20–35 per apostille or consular legalization)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traducción jurada) of foreign-language corporate and UBO documents into Spanish (estimated 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn Translator (Traductor Jurado) appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAEC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approx. EUR 55–65 per page per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) application and consular processing fee per non-resident shareholder/administrator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Consulate in country of origin / Dirección General de la Policía (Ministry of Interior)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee (Tasa T-012) and quota fee per applicant

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual registered office and compliance address (domicilio social) – first three months of serviced office with mail handling and notification forwarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate (approx. EUR 90–140 per month for registered-address and mail-handling bundle)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation due diligence and AML/CFT compliance counsel: UBO piercing analysis, PEP and sanctions screening (OFAC/EU/UN), drafting of incorporation minutes, and filing coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External legal counsel / compliance firm admitted in Spain
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed-fee package for standard SL incorporation with enhanced AML review (EUR 1,000–1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening documentation and compliance package (bank KYC/UBO declarations, source-of-funds evidence, and relationship manager file) – non-refundable bank administrative fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish credit institution (e.g., Banco Santander, CaixaBank, BBVA, or digital entity with IBAN)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff / compliance processing fee; refundable in part upon successful onboarding (approx. EUR 150–200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for ministerial authorization involving sensitive name tokens (e.g., 'Internacional' or geographic terms), including administrative filing fees and counsel revision
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of the Presidency / competent administrative body and external counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee if triggered, plus hour-based counsel revision (approx. EUR 80–120)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital - LSC), Title II (Arts. 19-22: incorporation deed, registration, legal personality), Art. 4 (minimum capital), Chapters on the Management Body (Arts. 209-212); Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil) and Commercial Code Arts. 119-124.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, Madrid) for the corporate name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office for the statutory inscription (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) granted before a Spanish notary, followed by an application for inscription (inscripción) in the Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 (Art. 4 LSC) fully subscribed and fully paid up at constitution; the funds must be deposited in a blocked 'company in formation' bank account in a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by a bank certificate (certificado bancario de desembolso) attached to the deed, or substituted by a notarial deposit certificate or an expert report for non-cash contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN VOTE OF ALL FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF FASHION JEWELRY TIMEPIECES, S.L. (THE COMPANY) ON [DATE]. 1. SHARES AND CAPITAL: The entire share capital of EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 equal participating units of EUR 1.00 nominal value each, has been fully subscribed and paid in by the incorporators, and the subscription list and paid-in certificate are hereby approved and ratify the allocations set out in the deed of incorporation. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The Company's registered office is fixed at Calle Orense 12, 28020 Madrid, Spain, and all statutory notices shall be sent there. 3. OFFICERS: The administrative body appointed in the deed (sole administrator) is confirmed for an indefinite term, with powers of representation, bank signature, contracting, and tax filings. 4. CORPORATE ACTS: The administrator is authorized to open bank accounts, obtain the definitive tax identification number, register the Company in the Mercantile Registry, and perform all acts to launch the online retail activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of the corporate name (Certificación negativa de denominación social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid (electronic window: Sede Electrónica of the Registro Mercantil Central, https://www.rmc.es)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official application form with up to three alternative names in order of preference. The digital certificate is issued with an electronic signature and is valid for 3 months. Present the certificate to the notary before expiry. Foreign shareholders may act through representatives holding notarized, legalized (Apostille) and translated powers of attorney.
required_dossiers: Official application form for negative name certification (solicitud de certificación negativa)
List of up to three proposed corporate denominations
Passport or NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) copies of all incorporating shareholders
Payment receipt of the statutory fee (tasa/arancel)
Power of attorney and proof of capacity (if representatives act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name coincides with an existing one or is prohibited, the application is corrected and resubmitted with new alternative names; the fee is paid again per attempt and a fresh certificate is obtained. No further substantive remedy is available for a denied name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the corporate escrow account and deposit of the minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution (e.g., Banco Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank, Banco Sabadell) - private banking window, not a state body.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company in formation (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada en constitución) and deposit at least EUR 3,000. Obtain the bank certificate of paid-up capital indicating the subscribers, the amounts paid, and the account number. The certificate must be dated immediately before the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (certificado de denominación)
Draft by-laws (estatutos) and preliminary incorporation deed
NIE/passports of the founding shareholders
Beneficial ownership declaration (AML/KYC forms)
Proof of source of funds for compliance verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML queries, provide the requested economic substance statement, bank references and audited proof of funds. If the account is refused, open the account at another Spanish bank; the deposit requirement is unaffected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Delegación de Grandes Empresas or the competent provincial tax office; online via the Sede Electrónica (modelo 036).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Census Declaration (modelo 036) electing the provisional NIF regime for the company in formation, attaching the certified negative name certificate and the consent to carry out the activity. The resulting provisional NIF letter must be delivered to the notary for use in the deed.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 with the provisional NIF option marked
Negative name certificate (original or certified copy)
NIE/passport copies of all shareholders and beneficial owners
Copy of the draft deed and by-laws (when requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT suspends the application due to tax residence doubts, submit the corresponding Certificate of Tax Residence of the shareholders under the applicable double taxation treaty or a sworn statement of residence; a new submission can also be made with corrective data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (notaría) of the city of the registered office, authorized by the Colegio Notarial de Madrid.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary verifies the identity and capacity of the subscribing partners, the bank certificate of the relevant capital and the validity of the name certificate. The deed (escritura de constitución) includes the by-laws, the corporate object (online retail of jewelry, watches and fashion accessories under ISIC 4791), the registered office and the appointment of the sole administrator. After signature, the notary issues the first copy (primera copia) for the Mercantile Registry and the testimonies for tax filings.
required_dossiers: Valid negative name certificate (within 3 months)
Bank certificate of the paid-up capital deposit
Provisional NIF of the company issued by AEAT
NIE/passports of all founding shareholders
Draft by-laws (estatutos) and draft deed prepared by counsel
Witnesses (notary will identify if required by law)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a legal defect (e.g., defective object clause or capital allocation), the deed is suspended and corrected before signing; the parties execute the amended document before the same notary within the validity period of the name certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Liquidation of the Corporate Transactions Stamp Duty (ITP-AJD, modelo 600)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria of the Autonomous Community where the registered office is located (e.g., Agencia Tributaria de la Comunidad de Madrid) - tax administration of the Consejería de Hacienda.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 working days of the deed, file model 600 for the 'operaciones societarias' segment of AJD. Incorporation of enterprises with a share capital not exceeding EUR 1,000,000 is exempt from the tax under Law 2/2010, but the declaration must still be filed to obtain the exemption. Attach the notarial copy and the bank deposit certificate.
required_dossiers: Modelo 600 duly completed (AJD - operaciones societarias)
First or second copy of the incorporation deed
Bank certificate of the paid-up capital
Provisional NIF of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the exemption is rejected, the tax (1% of share capital or the autonomous rate of 0.75%-1.5%) is paid under protest and a rectification or refund application (solicitud de devolución de ingresos indebidos) is filed before the competent Consejería; alternatively, a recurso de reposición can be lodged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (Registro Mercantil de Madrid, Calle Príncipe de Vergara 94).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first certified copy (primera copia) of the deed plus the proof of the model 600 filing within two months from the deed date. The registrar formally examines the legality of the deed and, if satisfied, grants the inscription. The company acquires full legal personality as of the inscription.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of the deed of incorporation
Proof of payment or exemption of the ITP-AJD (modelo 600 stamped)
Application form for registration (escrito de inscripción)
Provisional NIF of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a notice of defects (nota de calificación), the requerido party must cure the defects within 30 days and resubmit; a gubernative appeal (recurso gubernativo) lies before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública against an adverse qualification, with the inscription retroactive to the filing date if successful.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalization of the definitive NIF, census regularization and employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for the definitive NIF and census; Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) for employer registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the inscription, file a new modelo 036 removing the provisional NIF mark and attaching the registration certificate (certificación de inscripción); the provisional NIF is converted into the definitive NIF. If the company will hire employees, register as an employer with the TGSS through the Sistema RED and obtain the employer contribution code (Código de Cuenta de Cotización).
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 (modification of census data)
Certificate of the inscription issued by the Mercantile Registry (hoja registral)
Provisional NIF document
For TGSS: model TA.6 application, copy of the deed, registration certificate and identification of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT refuses the definitive conversion, present the registration certificate physically or electronically; if the TGSS returns the employer application, correct the worker/activity data and resubmit within the statutory deadlines, or appeal to the TGSS provincial administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid (Municipal authority - Área de Gobierno de Medio Ambiente y Movilidad) for the municipal opening communication and premises compliance; for precious metal articles, the Centro Español de Metrología (CEM) and the competent hallmarking bodies under Ley 3/1992.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - online retail of jewelry, watches and fashion accessories (ISIC 4791) has no sector-specific industrial operating permit. Where physical premises (warehouse/office) are opened, a municipal 'Comunicación Previa de Apertura' or 'Licencia de Actividad' may apply under Ley 12/2012 on simplified licensing; compliance with Ley 3/1992 (hallmarking rules for articles containing precious metals) is required only if such articles are sold.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) and the competent regional environmental administration (Comunidad de Madrid - Consejería de Medio Ambiente)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal EIA - e-commerce warehousing and logistics for fashion jewelry and watches are not listed in the Annexes of Ley 21/2013 (Environmental Assessment), so no full Environmental Impact Study or abbreviated Environmental Authorization is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC thresholds apply to office/warehouse use; the operation must comply with municipal wastewater discharge by-laws, packaging waste producer obligations under Ley 7/2022 (including registration in the Registro de Productores de Producto where applicable), the packaging green-point fee regime (Ecoembes) for online sales shipments, and the WEEE/battery take-back obligations under Royal Decree 110/2015 for products placed on the Spanish market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance under Royal Decree 513/2017 (Reglamento de instalaciones de protección contra incendios) with the municipal fire certification for the premises; structural and electrical safety inspections for the registered office/warehouse; occupational risk prevention plan and health surveillance under Ley 31/1995 (PRL) with a preventive service; workplace first-aid and emergency equipment; the company is not subject to the Seveso III major-accident duties due to the low-risk retail activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor incorporating a Spanish SL obtains a provisional NIF from the AEAT immediately after execution of the public deed and registration in the Mercantile Registry, then files Form 036 before the start of any economic activity to receive the definitive NIF and declare the IVA and IAE census status. A non-resident entity supplying goods or services in Spain without a permanent establishment must apply for a Non-Resident NIF (NIF-NR) on Form 030 before the first supply and appoint a Spanish fiscal representative if AEAT so requires. A Spanish branch or permanent establishment of the foreign parent applies for its own NIF on Form 036, annexing the parent's certificate of tax residence, constitution documents, and board resolution appointing the permanent establishment representative. The same NIF is used for IS, IVA, customs, statistical, and payroll purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not provide a US-style check-the-box or pass-through election. An SL is irrevocably a resident capital company taxable under Impuesto sobre Sociedades at entity level. Optional elections relevant to the same structure include the Spanish group consolidation regime for groups that satisfy the voting thresholds (article 64 LIS), the ETVE holding-company regime for eligible Spanish holding entities only, and ordinary elections such as the simplified cash-basis IVA regime for small SMEs. Hybrid mismatch positions are strictly governed by ATAD transposition under LIS articles 15oct, 15non and 15decies; no unilateral hybrid election is permitted, and taxpayers must document any cross-border instrument with the tax file to prevent deduction/non-inclusion mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) - Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis threshold: any taxable economic activity in Spain requires IVA registration on the Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholders before commencement. For a non-established e-commerce operator, registration is triggered by the first importation or first supply located in Spain; the EUR 10,000 pan-EU distance-sales threshold is an EU OSS routing rule and not a Spanish VAT registration exemption once goods are in or imported into Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not operate an Italian-style real-time fiscal clearing stamp (cAI). Instead: (1) large taxpayers in the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) regime - annual IVA turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000 or consolidated groups returning monthly IVA - transmit invoice and transaction registers to AEAT through secured web services within 4 calendar days of accrual or invoice issuance; (2) Royal Decree 1007/2023 implementing Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) mandates software and electronic invoicing standards (Facturae format) for B2B invoices and Verifactu-compliant billing software, with phased enforceability from 2024-2025; (3) invoices to public authorities are submitted through the FACe platform in Facturae XML; (4) online jewelry/watches sellers must maintain interoperable e-invoice repositories and expose transaction dates, counterpart NIF/NIF-NR, amounts, and export customs numbers to AEAT on request; there is no AEAT pre-clearance or digital stamp per invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Spanish exporter of jewelry, watches, and fashion goods may apply a 0% IVA rate as an export (exempt with credit of input VAT under article 21 LIVA) if the goods are physically dispatched or transported to a non-EU destination by the seller, purchaser, or a third party, normally within three months of the supply, and if the customs export declaration is accepted by Spanish Customs. The exporter must prove the exit from EU customs territory by transport documentation and keep the export evidence in the accounting file. Intra-EU B2B dispatches to a customer with a valid EU VAT number are zero-rated under article 25 LIVA, supported by the customer's VAT number, transport evidence, and recapitulative statement Model 349. Ancillary freight and loading services physically performed in Spain on exported goods are exempt. Digital or offshore services to non-EU business customers are generally outside the scope of Spanish IVA under the place-of-supply rules and do not require a 0% rate, but must be documented by contract, customer residence/establishment evidence, and bank payment records; input VAT on costs directly attributable to exported or outside-scope supplies can be deducted to the extent allowed by pro-rata rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / e-DUA) accepted and released by Spanish Customs in the Export Control System (ECS), showing the third-country destination and export customs number

Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document evidencing physical exit of the goods from the EU customs territory to the non-EU country, including consignee details, loading date, and port/airport of departure
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103 or bank-signed certificate of payment) proving receipt and repatriation of the export consideration from the foreign buyer to the Spanish exporter
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT automatically cross-validates customs exit declarations (ECS), VAT returns (Model 303/390), marketplace seller reports from OSS, and inbound payment flows (SWIFT MT103) through its data warehouse. If the export zero-rating is not substantiated by the required customs and transport documents or if foreign proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day benchmark, the exemption is denied retroactively and IVA is assessed at 21% on the invoiced amount, plus late-payment interest (interés de demora) and proportional penalties under LGT articles 191-193. The penalty scale is 50%-100% for negligent omission, 100%-150% for fraudulent under-declaration or suppression of records, and criminal tax prosecution (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) can apply if the defrauded annual tax amount exceeds EUR 120,000. Because jewelry and timepieces are high-value, low-volume goods, AEAT applies particularly intensive scrutiny to artificial triangular shipments, temporary imports re-exported without IVA, and payouts through PSPs not reconciled with the export declaration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); operational foreign-trade and investment statistics are administered jointly with the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, under Law 19/2003 of 4 July on Capital Movements and Economic Transactions and Royal Decree 1816/1991 of 28 December on Economic Transactions with the Exterior.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a euro-area member and maintains no currency exchange controls: the euro is fully convertible, and both current-account flows (export/online-sale receipts, royalties, dividends, profit remittances) and capital-account flows (equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, liquidation proceeds) are liberalised under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Law 19/2003. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted at the FX and treasury level; the only frictions are (i) Spanish tax withholding on distributions (19% general non-resident rate, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or to the applicable treaty rate, usually 5-10%, under the relevant double-taxation treaty) and (ii) mandatory statistical and administrative filings to the Banco de España for resident/non-resident transactions reaching reporting thresholds: payment-service providers must capture transfer-level information for amounts equal to or greater than EUR 50,000; certain operations (for example external shareholder loans and guarantees) require an individual 'declaración de operación exterior' when the amount exceeds EUR 150,000; and an annual 'posición de activos y pasivos con no residentes' declaration applies when gross balances exceed EUR 1,000,000. The ISIC 4791 e-commerce jewellery/watch business is not in Spain's screened FDI sectors (defence, critical infrastructure, media, energy, personal-data platforms under Royal Decree-Law 8/2020 and 11/2020), so inbound equity and minority foreign ownership are fully admissible without prior authorisation, conversion, surrender, or licence burdens.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain repealed all export-proceeds surrender obligations upon full liberalisation of external transactions: exporters, including the SL's online jewellery/watch merchant, are not required to repatriate proceeds within any statutory deadline, are not compelled to convert receipts into euro, and may retain 100% of collections in foreign-currency settlement accounts or in Spanish-authorised e-money wallets. The mandatory nexus is documentation and statistics: (i) physical exportations are declared through the AEAT customs platform using the DUA/ECS (Export Control System) with a customs value consistent with the commercial invoice; (ii) intra-EU dispatches require Intrastat declarations annually when the dispatch value exceeds EUR 400,000; and (iii) every cross-border transfer executed via a Spanish intermediary is transmitted by that bank to the Banco de España balance-of-payments register when the amount meets the applicable capture threshold (EUR 50,000 per transfer; EUR 1,000,000 for gross position declarations). No conversion ratio, no foreign-exchange certificate, no central-bank authorisation of sales proceeds, and no penalty timeline apply beyond the standard AEAT VAT/CIT reporting calendar.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito para la Constitución) and Operational Treasury Account
Capital Escrow Account and Multi-currency Operational Treasury Account with dedicated FX and Trade Finance desk
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Current Account linked to RedSys/global acquiring and import-documentation services
Capital Escrow Account and Corporate Operational Account with SWIFT direct clearing
Operational Treasury Account with optional money-market and FX hedging suite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for Spanish-regulated electronic-money institutions and payment institutions (entidades de dinero electrónico/entidades de pago) holding a valid Banco de España licence (for example Monei, Bnext and RedSys-backed issuers); such domestic EMIs can lawfully provide IBANs, card acquiring, e-money floats and payout rails for the SL's e-commerce settlement. Their limitations are commercial rather than legal: they seldom offer meaningful FX lines, high-value watch-trade finance, commercial letters of credit, or the correspondent bank network of a tier-1 credit institution, so they should be used as secondary collection rails, not as the anchor treasury bank. Offshore digital EMIs (post-Brexit UK-licensed EMIs, Lithuanian, Polish, or other issuers without a branch in Spain) are legally constrained under PSD2 and Law 10/2010: they may not provide payment/e-money services to Spanish residents or receive settlement funds on behalf of a Spanish resident SL without a registered Spanish agency arrangement or a licensed branch filed with the Banco de España; UK EMIs that lost EU passporting rights after Brexit are therefore non-viable as a primary treasury bank. They may act only as settlement aggregators where contractually linked to a Spanish-authorised agent, and such use requires enhanced record-keeping to preserve the audit trail demanded by Spanish AML enforcement practice.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for a de-novo corporate account of an SL with non-resident founders under the enhanced due-diligence policy of the tier-1 Spanish banks: Santander, CaixaBank and Sabadell will require an in-branch interview of the legal representative and each beneficial owner; BBVA and Bankinter may accept fully remote video-KYC onboarding where the director is an EU resident and can present eIDAS-certified electronic identification (DNIe, Spanish Cl@ve or another qualified EU electronic-ID) and the full corporate pack is apostilled; however, any remote-only route is practically rejected for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced classification (jewellery/watch trade, cross-border flows, PSP settlement) unless the corporate desk grants a written exception. The mandatory capital deposit for the incorporation deed is transferred by the founders to the bank's special escrow account before the public notary; this step does not require every shareholder to appear if a notarial power of attorney (poder especial) is used, but foreign documents must be legalised (Hague Apostille) and translated by a sworn Spanish translator. The realistic blueprint for this entity: one physical trip to Madrid or Barcelona by the founder and beneficial owner; a notarised board resolution authorising the account opening; NIE/TIE certificates and passports of the shareholders; apostilled certificate of incumbency where a foreign parent exists; anticipated onboarding lead time of 2 to 4 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory-minimum capital (as low as EUR 3,000) with rapid high-value turnover in the first quarters; the bank scoring engine treats fast luxury-goods revenue growth as a SEPBLAC-relevant money-laundering indicator for the watch/jewellery sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escritura de constitución and Registro Mercantil certificate; NIE/TIE and foreign passports with apostille and sworn Spanish translation; detailed ISIC 4791 business plan showing the e-commerce ramp; signed platform agreements with Stripe and PayPal including merchant identification numbers and settlement terms; supplier proforma invoices and purchase orders from established EU/US watch and jewellery distribution houses; first-period VAT/Intrastat returns and customs DUA filings proving physical goods flow; IAE registration under epigraph 4791; shareholder source-of-wealth statement and prior bank reference letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement risk: aggregated payouts from Stripe/PayPal enter the operating account without an identifiable end-customer IBAN, which Spanish AML compliance units classify as third-party receipts requiring provenance proof and UBO-chain verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Order-ID-to-settlement reconciliation ledger matching PSP payout reports to the accounting system and delivery trackings; item-level VAT invoices for each sale; pseudonymised customer KYC and payment-instrument provenance log from the PSP; platform and PSP-master agreements showing the settlement methodology; PCI-DSS report of compliance for the merchant; internal policy on customer disputes, refunds and chargebacks; and monthly reconciliation certificates countersigned by the external asesor fiscal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk geography: sales to buyers or freight-forwarders in Latin America, the UAE, Turkey or other cash-intensive jurisdictions may trigger targeted-financial-sanctions screening and correspondent-bank reviews, because luxury watches and branded jewellery are classic high-value value-transfer goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Timestamped sanctions and PEP screening logs of every customer and wallet address, including the exact screening rule-base version; geoblocking and shipping-address verification evidence proving that orders from sanctioned jurisdictions were automatically rejected; customs documentation proving lawful export; customer declarations of lawful ownership and source of funds for high-ticket transactions; export-licence waiver letters confirming no dual-use applicability; and DTT references for Mexico, Panama, Colombia and the UAE demonstrating a genuine Latin-America/EMEA distribution strategy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs valuation and invoice-price variance: under-invoicing or over-invoicing indicators between declared export values and the higher retail margin typical for certified jewellery and fine watches may be reported by trade surveillance as suspicious flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete value-chain documentation: commercial invoices; purchase-ledger entries; exact customs DUA values; independent gemological appraisals (IGI/GIA where applicable); watch serial numbers and COSC-certification records; shipping and marine-cargo insurance; a margin-rationalisation note comparing acquisition cost, PSP fees, import duties and realized e-commerce retail price; Intrastat/VIES filings for intra-EU dispatches; and weekly inventory-valuation reports demonstrating that invoicing matches actual cash movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity with co-mingled shareholder loans and customer receipts: the alternation of offshore shareholder loan inflows and PSP receivables creates a comingled treasury that the account officer may perceive as a breach of the 'declaración del titular real' and 'origen de fondos' evidentiary duties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated registro de titulares reales and Registro Mercantil annotation for every change in shareholding; notarised shareholder loan agreements in Spanish and English with arm's-length interest and subordination clauses; Banco de España 'declaración de operación exterior' for the loan inflow where the threshold is met; bank statements of the lending shareholder with a source-of-wealth narrative; a treasury policy segregating customer collections from shareholder funding; and a quarterly internal UBO register signed by the directors and examined by the external auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions are wired by SWIFT MT103 to the SL's Spanish IBAN (format ES followed by two control digits and the 22-digit BBAN). The remittance must carry a structured reason-for-payment: 'capital contribution / aportación de capital para ampliación de capital social' for true equity, or 'shareholder loan / préstamo de socios' for debt funding. For transfers equal to or above EUR 50,000 the receiving bank captures the Banco de España statistical declaration before crediting; for amounts exceeding EUR 150,000 the bank issues an individual 'declaración de operaciones exteriores'. The corporate resolution and, where the capital is actually increased, the notarial deed of capital increase with Registro Mercantil filing must be delivered to prevent an uncommitted credit balance from being frozen as an invalid or unexplained remittance. FX conversion from USD, GBP or CHF should be pre-hedged with an FX forward or swap to lock the euro amount; no central-bank approval is required for the wiring itself. Compliance verification sequence: (1) bank receives the deed and beneficial-ownership statement; (2) bank records the non-resident shareholder's NIE/TIE and tax identification; (3) bank executes sanctions/PEP screening against the sending account; (4) after clearance, the funds are credited and, if applicable, reported as 'inversión exterior' in the Banco de España statistical model.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU suppliers are paid via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) using IBAN alone, with same-day settlement on the T2 layer and zero cross-border charges; the reverse-charge mechanism applies for intra-community goods. Non-EU suppliers (Swiss watch houses, USA/China jewellery manufacturers) are paid via SWIFT MT103 with the proper remittance information in field 70 identifying the invoice, purchase order and the commercial purpose (trade payment); the payment is executed at spot or against a booked FX forward where the exposure was pre-hedged. For high-value timepieces and branded gold, the prudent rail is a commercial letter of credit (sight or usance, confirmed for CHF/USD beneficiaries) opened through the Banco Santander or BBVA trade-finance desk, supported by proforma invoices, insurance certificates, weight/purity certificates for gold, and serial-number manifests for watches. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) and low-ticket supplier settlements via the anchor bank's supply-chain finance module are permissible alternatives. The treasury should keep a dedicated multi-currency (USD, CHF, GBP) account at the anchor bank containing only working capital exposed to those currencies, with the surplus held in euro to minimise conversion friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forwards (FX forward contracts) in EUR/USD and EUR/CHF to hedge imported watch and jewellery purchases, executed under the anchor bank's ISDA/CSA documentation where counterparty exposure arises
Foreign-exchange swaps (fx swaps/permutas de divisas) to manage euro working-capital cycles and to bridge PSP settlement balances denominated in USD or GBP

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin-American currencies relevant to the distribution model (EUR/ARS, EUR/MXN, EUR/UYU) where a deliverable interbank market is otherwise absent; permitted only against genuine commercial exposure and within a documented board-approved hedging policy

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS) used to refinance or synthetically convert shareholder loans denominated in USD/CHF into euro, protecting both coupon and amortisation cash flows against exchange-rate movements

Plain-vanilla currency options and collars (for example EUR-call/USD-put and EUR-call/CHF-put structures) purchased from tier-1 Spanish banks under EMIR clearing conventions where applicable, always supported by a documented underlying commercial exposure to avoid speculative classification

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly created entities and qualifying newly incorporated companies may generally apply 15% during the first tax period in which they obtain a taxable profit and the following tax period, subject to statutory conditions and exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created companies may apply a 15% rate for the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period. Qualifying start-up companies under the Startups Law may apply 15% for the first profitable period and the following three periods while qualifying status is maintained. Research, development and technological innovation deductions, employment-related incentives, capitalization reserves, and tax-loss utilization may reduce the effective rate. Dividend and capital-gain participation exemptions may apply, generally subject to a minimum 5% participation and one-year holding requirement, with a 5% reduction for related management expenses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades e Impuesto sobre la Renta de no Residentes, electronic filing through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters. A Spanish SL is generally subject to Modelo 200.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company closing on 31 December, the normal filing window is 1 July through 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing rules extend the deadline to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company tax identification number (NIF), legal name, registered address, tax period, financial year dates, legal form, and filing type, including original, substitute, or supplementary filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not file these fields for the Spanish SL. The Spanish SL files using its own NIF. The non-resident shareholder must maintain its foreign tax identification and Spanish tax-representation documentation where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting result before corporate income tax based on the approved statutory accounts and accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not substitute the non-resident parent's consolidated result or foreign accounting result. Include only the Spanish SL's properly recorded Spanish entity result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to the taxable base by reporting permanent and temporary positive or negative adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, financial limitation adjustments, exempt income, and related-party corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties must be supported by arm's-length pricing, beneficial-owner analysis, withholding documentation, and evidence of services or rights received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable base after statutory adjustments and apply available tax losses, subject to the applicable percentage limitations and the general EUR 1 million minimum offset threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent-company losses cannot be used by the Spanish SL. Spanish tax losses must be substantiated through accounting records, filed returns, and documentation demonstrating the underlying transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the relevant corporate income tax rate, including the general 25% rate or a qualifying preferential rate, and calculate gross tax before credits and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's residence does not by itself entitle the Spanish SL to a reduced corporate tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible domestic deductions, international double-tax relief, research and development incentives, employment incentives, and other statutory credits with supporting calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require evidence of foreign tax paid or accrued, legal entitlement, income attribution, and compliance with Spanish limitation rules. Treaty relief does not automatically convert into a corporate tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit Spanish withholding taxes, advance payments, and installments previously paid against the final corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish withholding certificates must identify the Spanish SL or other taxpayer to which the withholding relates. Parent-company foreign tax withheld abroad is not entered as a Spanish withholding credit without a specific legal basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Final settlement and payment or refund section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the final amount payable or refundable, payment reference, bank direct-debit details where used, and authorized filing or representative information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Electronic filing may require a Spanish digital certificate, authorized tax representative, or approved filing intermediary. Foreign directors should not use personal credentials unless properly authorized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose relevant related-party transactions, restructuring, financing, intellectual-property payments, and other international tax information where required by the applicable Modelo 200 schedules and related forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with the foreign parent, group treasury company, logistics entities, licensors, or payment-service affiliates must be reconciled to transfer-pricing records, invoices, contracts, and withholding returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with tax payable generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay, without a penalty, when filed voluntarily before a tax assessment; after twelve months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus statutory late-payment interest from month thirteen. Failure or incorrect filing may generate administrative penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, subject to culpability, concealment, and repeated-offense rules. Electronic filing failures may also be treated as filing failures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax installments, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installments, generally due 1-20 April, October, and December; the December filing is normally due 1-20 December rather than after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally payable during the first twenty calendar days of April, October, and December. The relevant calculation method is normally based either on the prior year's final tax liability or on the current-period taxable base, depending on statutory eligibility and mandatory-method rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter NIF, legal name, tax period, installment number, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files in its own name. A foreign shareholder's tax residence is not entered as the taxpayer residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify whether the installment is calculated under the prior-year tax-liability method or the current-period taxable-base method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use current-period figures only where the company is legally required or entitled to use that method; document exceptional transactions and group reorganizations affecting the calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the applicable base, statutory percentage, prior installments, and any legally permitted adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign parent-company profits and non-Spanish amounts not attributable to the Spanish taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the final installment payable and complete electronic payment or direct-debit instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payment account and electronic authorization are valid for the Spanish entity and retain the payment confirmation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally triggers the statutory late-payment surcharge regime. Incorrect or omitted installments may also produce compensatory interest and administrative penalties, and may affect the annual Modelo 200 settlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, Información de operaciones vinculadas y de operaciones y situaciones relacionadas con países o territorios considerados paraísos fiscales, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, where statutory reporting thresholds or relevant transactions apply.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the normal deadline is 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter NIF, legal name, tax-period dates, and filing details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL reports its own related-party transactions; the foreign parent is identified as the related counterparty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify transactions such as financing, services, purchases, sales, leases, transfers of assets, intellectual property, and restructurings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify transactions with foreign group companies by legal and economic substance, not merely by invoice label.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report counterparty identity, jurisdiction, transaction type, aggregate amount, and whether the transaction is an income or expense item.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use consistent gross or net reporting as required by the form and reconcile totals to the general ledger, invoices, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report transactions and holdings falling within the applicable Spanish statutory list or rules for non-cooperative jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain current jurisdiction classification before filing. Treaty residence alone does not eliminate reporting where specific anti-abuse or non-cooperative-jurisdiction rules apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or materially incorrect information may trigger fixed or proportional penalties under Spain's General Tax Law, with increased exposure where the omission prevents or obstructs tax administration or conceals related-party income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory conditions are satisfied, commonly including a qualifying corporate parent, minimum 5% participation or qualifying acquisition-value test, minimum one-year holding or holding commitment, subject-to-tax requirements, and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and verify treaty entitlement, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where relevant, minimum holding periods, and anti-conduit conditions. Apply the reduced treaty rate only where the payer can substantiate entitlement; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to seek a refund through the AEAT procedure. Maintain the residence certificate, ownership chart, dividend resolution, payment evidence, beneficial-owner analysis, treaty article, and withholding certificate. Treaty certificates should be current under AEAT practice and renewed when required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish domestic non-resident income tax withholding is generally 24% on Spanish-source royalties, interest, and other qualifying income, reduced to 19% for qualifying EU or European Economic Area recipients under applicable rules. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide exemption for qualifying associated companies meeting ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-owner, and anti-abuse requirements. Tax treaties commonly cap interest and royalty withholding at rates ranging from 0% to 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty and income category. Technical services, software, digital rights, trademarks, and bundled arrangements require separate characterization. Spanish VAT, permanent-establishment, and beneficial-owner issues must be analyzed independently.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain generally requires related-party transaction documentation, subject to statutory content and exemptions, unless the aggregate value of transactions with the same related person during the tax period does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length, with important exclusions and special rules for transactions involving real estate, intangible assets, securities, or specified tax regimes. A Master File is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to a group with consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 45 million. A Country-by-Country Report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million and is normally filed by the ultimate parent or designated surrogate entity. The relevant local-currency threshold is EUR 250,000 for the principal small-transaction documentation exemption.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods may be used where the listed methods cannot reliably determine an arm's-length result
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate UAE-style or standalone generic Economic Substance Regulations regime. Economic substance is nevertheless material under the Corporate Income Tax Law, transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership principles, anti-abuse provisions, controlled foreign company rules, the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework, treaty principal-purpose tests, and permanent-establishment rules. A Spanish SL conducting online jewelry and watch sales should maintain genuine Spanish functions, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, inventory or logistics control where claimed, decision-making, commercial risk, customer management, payment controls, and adequate capitalization. Conduit financing, royalty pass-throughs, artificial management charges, circular payments, and profit allocation inconsistent with actual functions are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of sales, false invoices, fictitious expenses, undeclared related-party income, or intentional understatement of the Spanish taxable base causing a tax loss exceeding EUR 120,000 for a tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud generally carries imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the amount defrauded, together with loss of public subsidies and tax benefits for a period of 3 to 6 years. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of 2 to 6 times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers who knowingly participate may incur criminal liability, civil restitution for unpaid tax and damages, disqualification, and confiscation. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed judicially in criminal proceedings. Imprisonment is possible only where the statutory criminal elements are established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT fraud and undeclared ecommerce sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to charge or remit Spanish VAT, misuse of OSS/IOSS procedures, false export evidence, suppression of online sales, incorrect place-of-supply treatment, or diversion of marketplace receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may include fixed penalties and proportional penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus interest and surcharges. Criminal liability may arise where the tax-fraud threshold is exceeded or organized fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable under the General Tax Law where they caused or failed to prevent the infringement, particularly during dissolution or non-compliance. Criminal participation can result in imprisonment, fines, restitution, and asset measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording invoices for services not received, inflated group charges, fabricated logistics costs, personal expenses, or unsupported marketing and consulting deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the expense, reassessment of corporate income tax and VAT, late-payment interest, and penalties generally based on the unpaid tax. False-document conduct may also constitute a criminal offense when connected with tax fraud or accounting falsification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, accountants, and authorized signatories may face civil recovery, administrative liability, professional sanctions, and criminal prosecution where they knowingly created or used false records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificial royalties, management fees, financing margins, inventory prices, or commission rates that shift Spanish ecommerce profits to a foreign affiliate without corresponding functions, assets, risks, or evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose compensating adjustments, deny deductions, apply withholding tax, charge interest, and impose transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Failure to provide required documentation can attract penalties based on transaction value or fixed statutory amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary tax liability where the company cannot pay and the statutory conditions are met. Deliberate profit diversion may support criminal tax-fraud allegations and civil claims by the company or creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, agency fees, or other Spanish-source amounts to foreign recipients without withholding, without validating treaty residence, or by applying an EU exemption to a conduit or non-beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties. The foreign recipient may also face Spanish non-resident tax exposure where treaty or domestic relief is unavailable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary liability for knowingly approving non-compliant payments or failing to maintain withholding controls. Criminal liability requires additional statutory elements such as intentional tax fraud above the criminal threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaring jewelry or watches, undervaluing imports, using false country-of-origin statements, importing counterfeit branded goods, or splitting shipments to evade customs controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include customs debt, seizure, forfeiture, destruction of goods, administrative fines, loss of customs simplifications, trademark damages, and criminal prosecution for serious intellectual-property or customs offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face civil damages, confiscation, and criminal fines or imprisonment where intentional counterfeiting, smuggling, or aggravated customs fraud is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, concealing beneficial owners, failing customer due diligence where obliged, ignoring suspicious transactions, or structuring cash payments to avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements can result in substantial corporate fines, potentially up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover for serious cases and up to EUR 10 million or 10% of annual turnover for very serious cases, together with public reprimand, authorization consequences, and management disqualification. Cash payments involving a business or professional are generally restricted above EUR 1,000; the limit is generally EUR 10,000 where the payer is a non-resident individual not acting as a business or professional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and officers may receive personal fines, temporary disqualification, and civil liability. Criminal money-laundering liability may involve imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and judicial measures. Travel bans are not automatic and require judicial or statutory authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominee owners, circular shareholder loans, undocumented management arrangements, dormant entities, or foreign holding companies to conceal the person controlling the Spanish SL or the recipient of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include denial of treaty and participation exemptions, controlled foreign company or anti-abuse adjustments, tax reassessment, AML penalties, beneficial-owner reporting breaches, and criminal liability for fraud, money laundering, or document falsification where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto controllers may face civil restitution, tax liability, asset confiscation, disqualification, and imprisonment if criminal offenses are proven. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced solely because the entity is closely held.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining incomplete ledgers, deleting platform records, falsifying annual accounts, backdating contracts, concealing inventory, or submitting inconsistent accounting and tax data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible consequences include rejection of tax deductions, accounting penalties, tax reassessment, refusal of insolvency protection, commercial-register consequences, and criminal accounting or document offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability to the company, shareholders, creditors, and tax authorities, as well as criminal fines or imprisonment where intentional falsification or insolvency-related misconduct is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring assets to related parties, paying shareholder loans ahead of creditors, stripping inventory, continuing to trade while insolvent, or repatriating cash when statutory duties to creditors have arisen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include clawback, insolvency disqualification, director liability for the insolvency deficit, damages, asset recovery, and criminal insolvency offenses in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency deficit, return transferred assets, pay civil damages, and bear criminal fines or imprisonment. Judicial travel restrictions may be imposed in insolvency or criminal proceedings where legally justified.
